elasticsearch.attr.WorkflowId.answers: the run a dispatch-scoped record belongs to -- ExecutionLogScope.BuildScope, rides every record ProcessDispatchHandler writes for the hop whether or not that record's own template names it. Renders "D" (hyphenated), matching the L2 key format
elasticsearch.attr.WorkflowId.never_for: formatting it like CorrelationId ("N", no dashes) -- this id renders "D" (hyphenated); CorrelationId is the only id in this scope family that renders differently, and the two must never be pasted into each other's queries

elasticsearch.attr.StepId.answers: the step's position in the graph for a dispatch-scoped record -- ExecutionLogScope.BuildScope, rides every record the hop writes. Renders "D" (hyphenated)
elasticsearch.attr.StepId.never_for: formatting it like CorrelationId ("N", no dashes) -- this id renders "D" (hyphenated)

elasticsearch.attr.ProcessorId.answers: which processor ran a dispatch-scoped record -- ExecutionLogScope.BuildScope, rides every record the hop writes. Renders "D" (hyphenated). Not the same field as the Prometheus resource label of a similar name: that one is camelCase processorId and present only on a processor host's metrics
elasticsearch.attr.ProcessorId.never_for: formatting it like CorrelationId ("N", no dashes) -- this id renders "D" (hyphenated)

elasticsearch.attr.ExecutionId.answers: the execution a dispatch-scoped record belongs to -- ExecutionLogScope.BuildScope, omitted (not zeroed) on an entry dispatch, which has none. Renders "D" (hyphenated)
elasticsearch.attr.ExecutionId.never_for: formatting it like CorrelationId ("N", no dashes) -- this id renders "D" (hyphenated); also never assume its absence means the field was lost -- an entry dispatch genuinely has no execution id

elasticsearch.attr.EntryId.answers: the L2 key a dispatch-scoped record reads (on a dispatch) or writes (on a processed-data branch) -- ExecutionLogScope.BuildScope, omitted for a source step, which has none. Renders "D" (hyphenated)
elasticsearch.attr.EntryId.never_for: formatting it like CorrelationId ("N", no dashes) -- this id renders "D" (hyphenated); also never compare an EntryId from a dispatch record to one from a processed-data record as if they meant the same direction -- one is the key read, the other the key written

elasticsearch.attr.CorrelationId.answers: the cross-boundary correlation id echoed to HTTP clients in X-Correlation-Id and carried onto every bus record the request caused -- CorrelationKeys.Render. Renders "N": 32 lowercase hex characters, no dashes
elasticsearch.attr.CorrelationId.never_for: formatting it like a WorkflowId/StepId/ProcessorId/ExecutionId/EntryId ("D", hyphenated) -- this is the one id in the whole log schema that renders differently. A query using the hyphenated form returns zero hits and reads as "no records for this run", not as a format mismatch

elasticsearch.attr.ElapsedMs.answers: a per-event elapsed-time figure logged by HandoffDispatched, StepReturned, BranchCompleted and AdvancedSuccessors -- worth trusting over an interpolated histogram quantile at coarse resolution, since it is the exact value rather than a bucket edge
elasticsearch.attr.ElapsedMs.never_for: current state -- ES is history, and this is only present on the specific templates that name {ElapsedMs}, not on every record

elasticsearch.attr.SuccessorCount.answers: the fan-out width on AdvancedSuccessors -- how many successors one branch advanced, paired with {ElapsedMs} on the same record for the width and its cost together
elasticsearch.attr.SuccessorCount.never_for: current state -- ES is history, and this is only present on AdvancedSuccessors records

elasticsearch.attr.Result.answers: a step's verdict, on EntryStepCompleted and TerminalCompleted -- what an investigation reads to learn whether a step succeeded, without substring-matching the rendered body text for a weaker second spelling of the same fact
elasticsearch.attr.Result.never_for: current state -- ES is history; and never for a step whose template does not carry {Result} -- StepReturned and BranchCompleted report elapsed time only, not an outcome

elasticsearch.attr.Label.answers: one of the two config values AuthorConfig logs a step as having actually run with
elasticsearch.attr.Label.never_for: the config schema itself -- that is the processor's ConfigSchemaId in Postgres, not this record

elasticsearch.attr.Number.answers: the other of the two config values AuthorConfig logs a step as having actually run with
elasticsearch.attr.Number.never_for: the config schema itself -- that is the processor's ConfigSchemaId in Postgres, not this record

elasticsearch.attr.NextStepId.answers: one hand-off's destination step, on HandedOff
elasticsearch.attr.NextStepId.never_for: current state -- ES is history, only a record of one past hand-off

elasticsearch.attr.NextProcessorId.answers: one hand-off's destination processor, on HandedOff
elasticsearch.attr.NextProcessorId.never_for: current state -- ES is history, only a record of one past hand-off

elasticsearch.attr.NextEntryId.answers: one hand-off's destination L2 entry key, on HandedOff
elasticsearch.attr.NextEntryId.never_for: current state -- ES is history, only a record of one past hand-off

elasticsearch.attr.Queue.answers: which queue a fault-window record names -- StoreUnreachable, RefusingAndParking, RefusingNotParked, SendFailedReturning, ConsumptionPaused and ConsumptionAdmitted all carry it
elasticsearch.attr.Queue.never_for: attributing a StoreUnreachable/RefusingAndParking/RefusingNotParked/SendFailedReturning record to one run -- at that point in the code the ids are still undecoded bytes; only the queue name is known

elasticsearch.attr.Type.answers: the message type on a fault-window record -- RefusingAndParking, RefusingNotParked and SendFailedReturning all carry it
elasticsearch.attr.Type.never_for: attributing the record to one run -- at that point in the code the ids are still undecoded bytes

elasticsearch.attr.Reason.answers: why the AMQP channel shut down, on ChannelShutDown
elasticsearch.attr.Reason.never_for: current state -- the channel may already have reopened by the time this is read

elasticsearch.attr.WorkflowCount.answers: how many workflows the orchestrator hydrated from L2 before admitting its consumer, on OrchestratorHydrated
elasticsearch.attr.WorkflowCount.never_for: any other role's startup -- this template, and this attribute, is orchestrator-unique

elasticsearch.attr.timestamp.answers: @timestamp: when the record was written, arriving as either an ISO-8601 string or epoch milliseconds with a fractional part -- both map to the same date field
elasticsearch.attr.timestamp.never_for: assuming only one wire shape -- handling just one form works until a build that writes the other one ships

elasticsearch.attr.body_text.answers: body.text: the rendered message text, with every placeholder substituted -- one bucket per distinct rendering, unlike attributes.{OriginalFormat} which is one bucket per template
elasticsearch.attr.body_text.never_for: counting occurrences of a message shape -- rendered text varies per event (a duration, an id); group by attributes.{OriginalFormat} instead

elasticsearch.attr.original_format.answers: attributes.{OriginalFormat}: the unsubstituted template text -- what every elasticsearch.<TemplateName> surface in this catalog searches by, and the field templates() catalogues one value per
elasticsearch.attr.original_format.never_for: reading the rendered values out of it -- it is the template shape, not the substituted text; that is body.text

elasticsearch.attr.service_name.answers: resource.attributes.service.name: which role wrote the record -- filtering on a template alone is not enough for a template every service writes, such as HostShuttingDown
elasticsearch.attr.service_name.never_for: picking out one replica of a role -- every replica of the same role shares one service.name; use resource.attributes.service.instance.id for that

elasticsearch.attr.service_instance_id.answers: resource.attributes.service.instance.id: the replica identity on the log resource -- InstanceId.Resolve(), the same identity a replica's liveness key and reply queue use. This is the field a per-replica question must group on; resource.attributes.service.name alone cannot distinguish two replicas of the same role
elasticsearch.attr.service_instance_id.never_for: expecting it to vary per record within one process -- it is a resource attribute, materialised once when the log provider is built, so it is constant across every record this process writes

elasticsearch.attr.source.answers: resource.attributes.Source: the application type stamped on the resource -- worker or webapi (AddBaseConsoleObservability/AddBaseApiObservability's source parameter). Deliberately coarser than service.name: it says what shape of process wrote the record, not which role it played
elasticsearch.attr.source.never_for: distinguishing which role emitted a record -- that is resource.attributes.service.name; every processor, orchestrator, and keeper alike reports Source=worker

elasticsearch.attr.scope_name.answers: scope.name: the .NET logger category name the record was written through
elasticsearch.attr.scope_name.never_for: identifying which role wrote the record -- that is resource.attributes.service.name; the logger category is a code-location detail, not a deployment identity
